title: A Protocol for the Orbit
premise: Orsen Villalobos is a clone of a murdered fleet negotiator, created to keep the peace treaty between two rival fleets alive by impersonating the original. When colony children begin sharing dreams that contain fragments of the original's memories—leaked through an experimental neural archive Orsen unknowingly carries—the truth of the murder and the fraudulent treaty threatens to surface. Orsen must choose between preserving the lie that keeps two armed fleets from open war and exposing the truth about who killed her original: the treaty's own architect. In the end, Orsen confesses everything to both fleets, and the children's shared dream becomes the foundation of a new, honest accord—with Orsen finally accepted as herself rather than a copy.
about_author: Mirabel Okonkwo is a former orbital logistics dispatcher who spent six years coordinating cargo runs between asteroid colonies before turning to fiction full-time. She writes character-driven science fiction about identity, labor, and the families people build in the cold dark between worlds.

chapters.title: Deadweight
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A routine cargo haul through contested orbit establishes her careful, invisible life: forged credentials, memorized mannerisms of the dead original, and a strict rule against attachment. When she docks at Halcyon Colony, a child stares at her and says, 'You dream in blue.' Emotional beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream Together
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Orsen and Naya, a colony schoolteacher. Eleven children describe identical dreams—a white room, a woman's voice counting down, blood on glass. Naya recognizes details no one should know. Orsen realizes with horror they're describing her own fragmented memories. Emotional beat: creeping dread and denial.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Dead Woman
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. She audits her own neural archive, discovering corrupted memory blocks she was told were standard cloning artifacts—including the night of the original's murder. Her handler, Vess, warns her to stay silent; the treaty depends on 'Villalobos continuity.' Emotional beat: isolation, the weight of borrowed identity.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Naya's POV. The Meridian and Ashfall fleets arrive for the annual treaty renewal, warily sharing Halcyon's docks. Naya watches Orsen perform the original's diplomatic role flawlessly—and notices one fleet commander flinch at her face. Emotional beat: suspicion taking root; loyalty to her students versus caution.

chapters.title: What the Dream Knows
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. She secretly interviews the children, and their pooled dream-fragments reconstruct a memory she doesn't have: the original arguing with someone trusted, a syringe, a signature on a falsified manifest. The murderer was inside the treaty delegation. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: The Handler's Hands
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Orsen traces the falsified manifest to Vess, but before she can act, Vess accelerates the plan: a memory-wipe of the children disguised as a medical quarantine. Naya hides three students in the cargo hold of Orsen's ship. Emotional beat: betrayal, and the first true choice Orsen makes as herself.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Fleeing with the children through debris fields while both fleets mobilize over the 'missing' colonists, Orsen teaches them her trade—cargo straps, burn calculations—and something like family forms in the hold. The children's dreams grow clearer: they now remember the killer's voice. Emotional beat: found family forged under fire.

chapters.title: Continuity Error
chapters.summary: Naya's POV. Cornered at a derelict relay station, Orsen broadcasts nothing; instead she lets the children transmit the shared dream directly into both fleets' comm channels. Every crew hears the memory of the murder at once. Vess's voice is unmistakable. Emotional beat: terror turning to catharsis—the truth escaping all control.

chapters.title: The Confession Protocol
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Facing both fleets' guns, Orsen confesses everything: she is a clone, the treaty was signed by a dead woman's ghost, and Vess killed the original to protect his monopoly on the peace itself. Vess attempts to trigger her kill-switch failsafe—but the children's presence has overwritten it. Emotional beat: the climax—truth offered at gunpoint, survival by connection.

chapters.title: A Protocol for the Orbit
chapters.summary: Split POV, then collective. Months later, the fleets draft a new accord built on transparency, with the children's shared dream archived openly rather than hidden. Orsen signs it under her own name—not Villalobos, but a new one the children chose for her. Naya watches her stay docked at Halcyon, finally visible. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not inherited.
